findings.title: Local cache entry is written before the limit check, so a rejected device gets in on its next request
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` calls `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, ...)` (line 87) before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (line 93). When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the cache key stays set. For the next 29 minutes (`localcache.New(29*time.Minute, ...)`, line 42), every later request from that device hits the early `return nil` at line 83-84. `TagDevice` then returns nil, and `Anonymous.Authenticate` (client.go:44-58) returns an anonymous identity. Only the first request of a device over the limit is refused. A page reload lets it in, and nothing records it in the DB. Fix: set the cache entry only after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds, or delete it when the call fails.

findings.title: pkg/server/wire.go still registers ProvideAnonDBStore, whose new int64 parameter has no provider
findings.body: `ProvideAnonDBStore` now takes `(db.DB, int64)`. `pkg/server/wire.go:374-375` still lists `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and binds `anonstore.AnonStore` to it. Nothing provides an `int64`. `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` now builds the store itself (impl.go:43), and no other wire consumer of `anonstore.AnonStore` exists, so the provider is also unused. Wire rejects both a missing input and an unused provider, so regenerating `wire_gen.go` (which the Go build does) should fail. Remove the two lines from wire.go.

findings.title: Requests without X-Grafana-Device-Id skip the device limit entirely
findings.body: `TagDevice` returns nil when the `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header is missing (lines 119-121) or the IP cannot be parsed (lines 125-128). `Authenticate` then grants anonymous access with no limit check. The device ID is also chosen by the client, so any client can reuse an ID that is already registered. Is `device_limit` meant only as a usage counter for the UI, or as an access limit? If it is an access limit, a request without the header should probably be refused once the limit is reached.

findings.title: Separate count and insert let concurrent new devices go over the limit
findings.body: `CountDevices` (line 110) and the upsert (lines 149-153) run in separate sessions with no lock or transaction. Several new devices arriving at once, or several Grafana instances in HA, can all read `count < limit` and all insert. The limit is then exceeded. If the limit must be exact, run the count and insert in one transaction, or use a conditional `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < ?`.

findings.title: Device tagging moved from a goroutine onto the request path, using the request context
findings.body: The upsert used to run in a goroutine with its own 2-minute `context.Background()` timeout. With `device_limit` set, it now runs synchronously on the request path, together with a `COUNT(*)` over `anon_device`, on every local-cache miss. This applies even when no limit is configured. The write also uses the request `ctx`. If the client disconnects, the write is cancelled, but the cache key was already set (impl.go:87), so that device is not tagged for the next 29 minutes. Consider keeping the async path when `AnonymousDeviceLimit == 0`.

findings.title: Limit test does not cover a known device updating while the store is at its limit
findings.body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only checks that a second, new device is rejected. It never re-submits the first device (`32mdo31deeqwes`) after the limit is reached. That is the path `updateDevice` exists for, and it is what keeps existing users working. There is also no `TagDevice`/`Authenticate` test with a limit, which would have caught the local-cache bypass in impl.go:87.

findings.title: New `device_limit` option is not documented in conf/defaults.ini or sample.ini
findings.body: The other `[auth.anonymous]` keys, such as `hide_version`, are listed in `conf/defaults.ini:592` and `conf/sample.ini:581`. `device_limit` is not, so operators have no way to find it.

findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit is typed as possibly undefined, but the backend always sends a number, and the frontend never reads it
findings.body: `FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit` is an `int64` with no `omitempty` (frontend_settings.go:195). The boot data therefore always contains a number, 0 when the option is unset, never `undefined`. With the `= undefined` initializer and no annotation, TypeScript also infers the class field's type as `undefined`. Nothing under `public/` reads the field. Consider `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined`, or `= 0`, or leave the field out until a consumer exists.

contracts.action: Anonymous.Authenticate now calls TagDevice synchronously and fails authentication on ErrDeviceLimitReached
contracts.equivalent_path: The old code ran TagDevice in a goroutine with a 2-minute background timeout and only logged errors
contracts.before_after: Before: tagging was fire-and-forget. After: tagging blocks the request, and ErrDeviceLimitReached makes Authenticate return an error. The local cache is set before the store call, so a rejected device is let in on later requests.
contracts.visible_effect: The authn service joins the error and tries the remaining clients. contexthandler stores it in LookupTokenErr and the request continues unauthenticated, so the user is redirected to login or gets a 401.
contracts.failure_mode: After one rejection, the cache key makes TagDevice return nil for 29 minutes, so the limit is not enforced (finding on impl.go:87). Other DB errors are logged and the request continues anonymously.

contracts.action: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts active devices and, when at the limit, only updates existing ones
contracts.equivalent_path: usageStatFn and the admin stats use CountDevices with the same 30-day window
contracts.before_after: The count and the update/insert run in separate sessions, with no transaction around them
contracts.visible_effect: A new device over the limit gets ErrDeviceLimitReached; an existing device updated in the last 30 days is updated normally
contracts.failure_mode: Concurrent inserts can push the count over the limit. MySQL reports matched rows rather than changed rows because of clientFoundRows=true, so an update that changes nothing is not mistaken for an unknown device.

contracts.action: ProvideAnonDBStore signature gains a deviceLimit int64 parameter
contracts.equivalent_path: pkg/server/wire.go:374-375 registers the provider and its interface binding
contracts.before_after: wire.go is unchanged and still lists the provider
contracts.visible_effect: Wire code generation, and therefore the build
contracts.failure_mode: No int64 provider exists, and the provider is now unused, so wire generation should fail

summary: The device limit doesn't hold as written. `tagDeviceUI` caches the device key before the store's limit check, so a device turned away once gets anonymous access on every request for the next 29 minutes. Also, `pkg/server/wire.go` still registers `ProvideAnonDBStore`, which now takes an `int64` that nothing provides, so wire generation should break. Smaller points: requests without the device-ID header skip the limit, a race lets concurrent new devices go over it, tagging now runs on the request path, the limit test is thin, and the new `device_limit` option isn't in the config files.
